newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mandarin Oriental 1996 profits rise to US$60.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mandarin Oriental 1996 profits rise to US$60.1 mln.

text.p: Hotelier Mandarin Oriental International Ltd said on Wednesday net attributable profits rose to US$60.1 million for the year to December 31, 1996, compared to US$53.7 million in 1995.
The group, which operates 12 deluxe and first-class hotels mainly in the Asia-Pacific region, was also upbeat about prospects for 1997.
Positive trends at the group's Hong Kong and Manila hotels had continued into 1997 and it anticipated overall improvement in its other Asian hotels, chairman Simon Keswick said in a statement.

Keswick said he expected a positive contribution from the Hyde Park hotel in London in its first full year within the group. Mandarin Oriental paid 86 million sterling for the Hyde Park in November 1996.
"The outlook for 1997 is encouraging," Keswick said.
Keswick said the group's two Hong Kong hotels, its flagship Mandarin Oriental and The Excelsior, had benefited from the strength of the territory's hotel sector.

Occupancy rates at the Mandarin Oriental had risen to 85.4 percent for the first two months of 1997, compared to 72.1 percent in the same period last year, managing director Robert Riley told Reuters by telephone.

According to the profit and loss account, Hong Kong and Macau operations contributed the lion's share of the US$81.5 million in total profits before interest and tax in 1996, weighing in with US$61.6 million between them.
Hong Kong's hotel sector is expecting strong demand in 1997, largely due to a number of one-off events.

The territory is hosting the World Cup Sevens Rugby tournament this coming weekend and expects a surge in visitor arrivals to witness its return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years under British rule.
Hong Kong is also hosting a World Bank-International Monetary Fund meeting in September.
Mandarin Oriental is 51 percent owned by Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd.
